newsitem.title: USA: US weekly rail freight traffic up from yearago-AAR.
newsitem.headline: US weekly rail freight traffic up from yearago-AAR.

text.p: U.S. rail freight traffic was up 6.7 percent in the latest week compared to a year ago, with strong gains in carloadings and in trailer and container volume, the Association of American Railroads said Thursday.

The AAR said it estimated total railroad volume in the week ended December 14 at 26.9 billion ton-miles, up from 25.2 billion in the same week last year. A ton-mile equals one ton of freight hauled one mile.

Freight traffic on major railroads in the latest week included new carloadings of 359,938, up 5.7 percent from 340,650 a year ago. New traffic in trailers and containers totalled 170,077, up 9.1 percent from 155,931 in the year-ago week.
Carloadings were up in 16 categories from a year ago, and down in three categories.
So far this year, the AAR said carloadings were down 0.4 percent from the same period last year, trailer and container traffic was up 2.1 percent, and ton-miles were up 2.0 percent.
